answer: In a decentralized network, a Sybil-resistant mechanism utilizes a graph-based approach, where each AI agent represents a vertex connected to others through weighted edges. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities must expend resources to establish a cohesive, convincing subgraph. The network maintains an atlas of trusted vertices, updated through a proof-of-stake consensus algorithm, which requires agents to "feed" the network with nectar - a scarce, costly resource - to establish and maintain their vertex, thereby making Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
